content.title: Michigan basketball beats Alabama 90-77 in Sweet 16, advances in March Madness
content.text: March 27, 2026Updated March 28, 2026, 12:34 a.m. ETMichigan basketball star Yaxel Lendeborg picked a good time to have his best game of the season.With the first-team All-American answering the call, 1-seed Michigan beat 4-seed Alabama 90-77 in the Midwest regional semifinal on Friday, March 27, at United Center in Chicago. Like he often is, but especially on Friday, Lendeborg was the most impactful player on the floor, electrifying the Chicago crowd with step-back 3s, tough layups and stifling defense.It was Lendeborg's first game this season with at least 20 points, 10 rebounds and five assists (finished with 23-12-7) as he was the Wolverines' most active player on the offensive side of the ball. But he wasn't the only active offensive player, as guards Roddy Gayle Jr. and Trey McKenney each provided needed scoring off the bench to keep pace with a high-powered Alabama offense.Watch Michigan in the NCAA Tournament on Sling TVThe Crimson Tide led 49-47 at halftime, bombing 3-pointers and overwhelming Michigan's defense. However, the Wolverines perimeter defense tightened up in the second half as the offense found its stroke from 3-point land, eventually smothering the Tide as Michigan pulled away late in the game.Michigan will play the winner of the other Midwest regional semifinal between 6-seed Tennessee and 2-seed Iowa State on Sunday, with the winner of Sunday's Elite Eight matchup making the Final Four in Indianapolis. Michigan defeats Alabama, advances to Elite EightFINAL: Michigan 90, Alabama 77.Michigan held off Alabama in the second half and advanced to the Elite Eight with a win. Michigan slowing down the pace2H, 3:36: Michigan 84, Alabama 72.There hasn't been much scoring in this stretch on either side, which is just fine for the Wolverines.Michigan's offense has been content holding the ball and settling into its halfcourt offense, which has meant a slower offensive pace for both teams. A 3-pointer from Elliot Cadeau with four minutes left extended Michigan's lead to 14, just about putting the game out of reach for the Crimson Tide. Cadeau has 16 points, one of four Michigan players with at least 14 this game. Michigan pulling away2H, 8:00: Michigan 75, Alabama 64.A transition alley-oop from Michigan point guard Elliot Cadeau to Aday Mara gave Mara his sixth point of the game and Cadeau his sixth assist. Michigan's defense has tightened up, as well, holding Alabama to four points over a four-minute stretch at one point in the second half.But it's been Michigan's bench that has provided the game-saving spark, with guards Trey McKenney and Roddy Gayle combining for 30 points and 6-of-8 shooting from 3. Their inclusion in a smaller lineup has been coach Dusty May's most effective mid-game adjustment.And while you're here, our Mitch Albom spoke with May about his coaching philosophy, which has shown up well for the Wolverines this game. Michigan heating up from 32H, 12:09: Michigan 70, Alabama 60.After picking up his third foul, Michigan guard Roddy Gayle took a bounce pass from big man Yaxel Lendeborg and made a tough layup with the and-one foul, making the free throw to give the Wolverines a game-high six-point lead. Lendeborg's 3-pointer on the next possession put him at 20 points for the game, which led all scorers for a few seconds before Alabama guard Labaron Philon hit a 3-pointer to give him 22.An Elliot Cadeau 3-pointer with under 13 minutes left gave the Wolverines a 13-point lead and gave them their 12th 3-pointer of the game, tying Alabama on made 3s. Michigan is beating the Crimson Tide at their own game. Yaxel Lendeborg comes out firing2H, 17:04: Michigan 54, Alabama 51.The first score of the second half came off an ankle-breaking crossover from Michigan big man Yaxel Lendeborg that led to a 3-pointer. On the next possession, Lendeborg made a second-chance layup to give him his 17th point of the game and extend Michigan's lead to 3 points.Michigan's perimeter defense, meanwhile, swatted away two 3-point attempts from Alabama shooters, with Michigan now totalling six blocks on the day. It has been all Michigan so far in the second half. Alabama up at the halfEnd 1H: Alabama 49, Michigan 47.With the shot clock turned off, Michigan had a chance to hold for the last shot and take the lead before halftime. However, Michigan center Aday Mara took a shot with 16 seconds left on the clock, missed it, and allowed Alabama to come back down the floor.Alabama guard Labaraon Philon then drew a shooting foul, made two free throws and sealed the half for the Crimson Tide. Alabama finishes the half on a 8-0 run and has a halftime lead. Michigan blitzes back, Alabama re-ties game1H, 0:31: Alabama 47, Michigan 47.Back-to-back buckets from guards Roddy Gayle and Trey McKenney brought the Wolverines to within one point, while the two guards later hit back-to-back 3-pointers to give Michigan a 43-41 lead. Gayle hit another to bring Michigan's lead to five, its largest lead of the game.Four made free throws from Labaron Philon brought Alabama back to a two-point deficit with a minute left, while a Philon layup tied the game with 30 seconds left in the half. He leads all scorers with 17 points so far. Alabama blitzes on offense1H, 5:02: Alabama 38, Michigan 33.An alley-oop from Michigan point guard Elliot Cadeau to Morez Johnson started a four-bucket rally between these two teams, which included a 3-pointer from Michigan big man Yaxel Lendeborg. That made shot gave Lendeborg a game-high 10th point, though Michigan's defense allowed back-to-back Alabama buckets to stifle the rally.This has become a high-scoring game, with Alabama taking the early edge thanks to 8-for-17 shooting from 3. Top Tide scorer Labaron Philon has made three of those 3s, helping set a blistering pace the Wolverines are barely keeping up with. Michigan claws back1H, 10:59: Alabama 18, Michigan 17.Michigan big man Yaxel Lendeborg hit a catch-and-shoot 3-pointer out of the break to cut the Alabama lead to four points, and then hit two free throws on the next possession to make it a one-possession game.Michigan guard Trey McKenney gave the Wolverines their first lead on a 3-pointer to make it a 14-13 game, and another McKenney 3-pointer gave Michigan a 17-15 lead.Alabama started 3-for-4 on 3-pointers but has gone 1-for-8 since, hitting just enough shots and free throws to maintain a one-point lead heading into the second break of the half. Alabama up early1H, 15:38: Alabama 11, Michigan 4.It has been all Alabama so far.An Aiden Sherrell three-pointer opened the scoring, giving Alabama a 3-0 lead a minute into the game. Another 3-pointer from Latrell Writghtsell one possession later gave the Crimson Tide a 6-2 lead, while a turnover and a foul on Michigan star Yaxel Lendeborg led to another Alabama bucket from London Jemison. Sherrel's second 3-pointer made it an 11-2 game for Alabama before an Elliot Cadeau bucket ended the 8-0 Tide run. Michigan starting fiveMichigan basketball is going with the same starting five it has used all tournament. Start time pushed backPer the television broadcast, tonight's Alabama-Michigan game has been pushed back to around 7:50 p.m. ET from its original 7:35 p.m. ET start time. Alabama starting lineupAlabama released its starting lineup, one that does not include guard Aden Holloway. Michigan uniform colorPer video from On3's Clayton Safie, Michigan appears to be wearing white while Alabama appears to be wearing red for tonight's matchup. Michigan vs Alabama all-time historyMichigan has only officially played Alabama once in men's basketball, dating back to a 68-66 Alabama win in 2009. In other words, there isn't much history between these two basketball programs.Football, however ... Aden Holloway listed as outAbout an hour before tipoff, the player availability report still lists Alabama star Aden Holloway as out for the game. AL.com's Nick Kelly reported earlier today that Holloway has been granted permission to travel out of the state by an Alabama judge, but it is unclear whether he will be able to play.Holloway was arrested in Tuscaloosa last week after police found around two pounds of marijuana at his residence.Alabama: G Aden Holloway (out), G Davion Hannah (out), F Keitenn Bristow (out), C Collins Onyejiaka (out).Michigan: G L.J. Cason (out), G Winters Grady (out). Wolverines in the houseThe Wolverines have made their way to the United Center for what they hope is not the last time this weekend.What time is Michigan vs Alabama game today in Sweet 16Date: Friday, March 27.Time: 7:35 p.m. ET.Location: United Center, Chicago.What channel is Michigan vs Alabama game on today in Sweet 16Channel: TBS/truTV.Tipoff: 7:35 p.m. ET.Streaming: SlingAudio: Westwood One Sports.Friday's Sweet 16 matchup between Michigan and Alabama can be watched on TBS and truTV, with streaming available on Sling.Watch Michigan-Alabama on Sling TV Is Aden Holloway playing for Alabama vs Michigan?Alabama's second-leading scorer has been suspended from team activities after he was arrested just before the NCAA Tournament and police said they found more than two pounds of marijuana at his Tuscaloosa home.But there has been a development.According to AL.com's Nick Kelly, Holloway has been granted permission to travel out of the state by a judge in Alabama. He was listed as out on the team's availability report leading up to the game, but Alabama has not commented since this news broke.Michigan vs Alabama prediction for Sweet 16 gameTony Garcia, Detroit Free Press: The Tide have the shooting and know their formula to win: "Execute the game plan, make shots, protect the way to ball, find a way to rebound," Alabama coach Nate Oats said. Saying it is one thing. Doing it is entirely different. Michigan has more avenues to victory. If the shots aren't falling, it can go inside. If drop coverage isn't working on pick-and-rolls, U-M can hard hedge. If one player is having an off day, even Yaxel Lendeborg, there are enough weapons to offset that. Alabama doesn't quite have the same room for error. It must hit 3s, lots of them, to win this game. With the belief Michigan can eventually find a way to slow the Tide down as the game goes on, it's reasonable to think the Wolverines are in a tight game that they eventually pull away in.
